'''Cristina Perlas Parel''' (died April 10, 2011) was a [[Filipina]] statistician, the first Filipino to earn a doctorate in statistics, the former dean of the Statistical Center at the [[University of the Philippines]], and at the time of her death the only professor [[emeritus]] of statistics at the University of the Philippines.{{r|virola}} She was president of the Philippine Statistical Association in 1966 and 1969, and the first female president of the association.{{r|psai}}

==Biography==
Parel earned a B.S.E. from the [[University of the Philippines]]. She completed a master's degree in 1949{{r|regents}} and a doctorate in 1958 from the [[University of Michigan]]; her dissertation, supervised by {{ill|Paul S. Dwyer|de}}, was ''A Matrix Derivation of Generalized Least Squares Linear Regression with All Variables Subject to Error''.{{r|mgp}} She worked at the Statistical Center of the University of the Philippines from 1958 to 1984, and served as dean from 1969 to 1984.{{r|nscb}}

==Honors and awards==
In 1971, Parel was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}} She was one of five people designated in 1999 as "Pillars of the Philippine Statistical System".{{r|mijares}} She was presented with a plaque of recognition by the Philippine National Statistical Coordination Board in 2007.{{r|nscb}}
